questions.prompt: With --allowedTools "Read,Edit,Bash(node *)", which command can Claude run in the shell?
questions.explanation: Bash(node *) scopes shell access to commands starting with 'node'. npm, rm, and git don't match the prefix and are denied. Scoped Bash rules are the heart of least-privilege agent setups.

questions.prompt: In --permission-mode dontAsk, what happens when Claude tries a tool that is NOT in the allowed list?

options.text: The user gets a permission prompt
The call is denied automatically and Claude must adapt or explain it can't proceed
The call runs anyway with a warning

questions.explanation: dontAsk means no human in the loop: allowed tools run, everything else is silently refused. Perfect for headless automation — like this app, where there's no way to click approve mid-stream.

questions.prompt: You want Claude to review code and report issues WITHOUT changing anything. Best --allowedTools?
questions.explanation: A review needs to find and read files — nothing more. Granting Edit or unscoped Bash to a read-only job violates least privilege for zero benefit.

questions.prompt: Match the mode to a sensible use. Which pairings are right? (select all that apply)

options.text: Default prompting — exploring an unfamiliar repo where you want to see each action
acceptEdits — a refactor session where you trust file edits but want to approve commands
dontAsk with a tight allowlist — unattended automation like CI or this app's sandbox
dontAsk with all tools allowed — running an unknown repo's setup script overnight

questions.explanation: Looser modes demand tighter allowlists and safer environments. dontAsk + everything-allowed + unknown code + nobody watching (d) stacks every risk at once.
